summary.name: Jami
summary.one_liner: Jami is a free/libre, end-to-end encrypted, peer-to-peer communication app for messaging, calls, group chats and video conferences that does not require a central server.
use_cases: group chats and video conferences without third-party hosting
making SIP calls from a free app
chatting on a local network without internet
summary.what_it_does: Jami provides instant messaging, audio and video calls, group chats, and video conferences with rendezvous points hosted without third parties. It supports audio and video message recording, screen sharing, and media streaming. Communications are peer-to-peer and end-to-end encrypted with perfect forward secrecy, and the page says it complies with the X.509 standard. It can also function as a SIP client and offers a built-in extension platform. Users on the same local network can keep communicating when disconnected from the internet, and no personal information is required to create an account.
notable: Completely peer-to-peer, no server relays data between users
GNU project licensed under GPLv3 or later
Can function as a SIP client
Works on the same local network without internet access
caveats: The page says there will never be advertising, but it does not state a paid tier
Donation is requested to expand the free sharing service
